investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-07-14T00:26–00:33Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a schedulable state, so the eval contract was violated before any VM or agent identity could be established.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that label. The other four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving zero schedulable nodes for any new remote-agent pod. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never returned an agent identity, and the eval produced an empty evidence object, failing all four required-evidence assertions (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) defined in check-expectations.json line 256.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] The two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have their allocatable VM slots fully consumed by existing running remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. Preemption was attempted and found no victims, indicating all current occupants are non-preemptible.

[Likely] A node that previously held kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity was cordoned, drained, or removed from the cluster, reducing the pool from a larger count to exactly 2 nodes, both of which are now saturated.

[Possible] The node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod template was recently tightened or the matching node labels were removed from additional nodes, shrinking the eligible set to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes and making the 4 remaining nodes permanently ineligible.

[Possible] A quota or LimitRange on the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was lowered at the namespace or cluster level, reducing the effective per-node allocation below what the probe pod requests.

[Less likely] The eval runner itself submitted multiple concurrent probe pods (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime ran sequentially but close together), and the first pod consumed the last available VM slot before the siblings could schedule — though the timing spread (00:26–00:33) and the fact that all three failed with the same 'Insufficient' message makes simultaneous exhaustion the more consistent explanation.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the two capable nodes at the time of the eval run, the root cause would not be capacity exhaustion and a different scheduling or admission block would need to be investigated.

If the probe pod was never submitted to the cluster (e.g., the API call to create the remote agent failed before a pod was created), the scheduler message would not appear; its presence in the eval message confirms a pod was submitted and rejected.
If only one of the three sibling checks failed while the others passed, a transient single-pod scheduling blip rather than full capacity exhaustion would be the more likely explanation.

If the node affinity/selector on the pod template matched more than 2 nodes, the 'didn't match' count of 4 would be lower, suggesting the affinity is not the primary constraint and capacity exhaustion on the 2 matching nodes is the sole blocker.

If a passing run of remote-agent-create is observed shortly after this failure without any infrastructure change, it would suggest a transient capacity spike rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-14 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), and preemption cannot resolve the shortage. Because the remote agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never completed, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across all eligible nodes. Of the 6 nodes in the cluster, only 2 support the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are at capacity; the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector and are therefore ineligible. With no preemption victims available, every new remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state for the full eval window (~128–150 s), causing the eval runner to time out before createAgent returns, leaving all required evidence fields empty and triggering a contract validation failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

All three sibling checks report the identical scheduler message, confirming this is a cluster-level resource exhaustion rather than a single-pod anomaly.

[Secondary] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes — the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes carry, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 already-saturated nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive, adding capacity elsewhere in the cluster would not help.

[Lower confidence] The node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods may have changed in a way that reduced the eligible node pool, but no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.

No evidence was collected by any check, meaning the agent pod never started and the runtime response contract was never exercised.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never returned an agent, and the expected-output contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were never populated. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents kata peer-pod node pool; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production user impact.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-07-14T00:26–00:33Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a schedulable state, so the eval contract was violated before any VM or agent identity could be established.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that label. The other four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving zero schedulable nodes for any new remote-agent pod. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never returned an agent identity, and the eval produced an empty evidence object, failing all four required-evidence assertions (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) defined in check-expectations.json line 256.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187: remote-agent-create is marked required:true with degradedAfterFailures:1, meaning a single failure triggers a degraded signal for the remote-agents feature
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have their allocatable VM slots fully consumed by existing running remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. Preemption was attempted and found no victims, indicating all current occupants are non-preemptible.

[Likely] A node that previously held kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity was cordoned, drained, or removed from the cluster, reducing the pool from a larger count to exactly 2 nodes, both of which are now saturated.

[Possible] The node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod template was recently tightened or the matching node labels were removed from additional nodes, shrinking the eligible set to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes and making the 4 remaining nodes permanently ineligible.

[Possible] A quota or LimitRange on the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was lowered at the namespace or cluster level, reducing the effective per-node allocation below what the probe pod requests.

[Less likely] The eval runner itself submitted multiple concurrent probe pods (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime ran sequentially but close together), and the first pod consumed the last available VM slot before the siblings could schedule — though the timing spread (00:26–00:33) and the fact that all three failed with the same 'Insufficient' message makes simultaneous exhaustion the more consistent explanation.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-14 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), and preemption cannot resolve the shortage. Because the remote agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never completed, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state was fully violated.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across all eligible nodes. Of the 6 nodes in the cluster, only 2 support the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are at capacity; the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector and are therefore ineligible. With no preemption victims available, every new remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state for the full eval window (~128–150 s), causing the eval runner to time out before createAgent returns, leaving all required evidence fields empty and triggering a contract validation failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — no capacity for a new peer-pod VM, and preemption found no evictable victims. All three sibling checks report the identical scheduler message, confirming this is a cluster-level resource exhaustion rather than a single-pod anomaly.

[Secondary] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes — the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes carry, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 already-saturated nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive, adding capacity elsewhere in the cluster would not help.

[Tertiary] A concurrent workload spike or leaked/stuck peer-pod VMs may be holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, preventing new allocations even if overall cluster compute is available.

[Lower confidence] The node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods may have changed in a way that reduced the eligible node pool, but no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.
